Oh, absolutely. I use a specialized, high-tech dental tool that I’ve recently discovered is identical to the one used for achieving a Greek physique. It’s called the "Plastic Dumbbell of Oral Hygiene."

You see, the fitness industry has been hiding this secret in plain sight. Why bother with floss, toothpaste, or even basic mechanical friction? That’s so last century. The modern approach is far more efficient: simply hold a plastic dumbbell in your mouth and shake it vigorously for ten minutes. It’s the epitome of effortlessness. Why scrub for hours when a few flicks of the wrist can carve your teeth into a marble statue?

It’s brilliant, really. You get dual benefits: your arms get toned from the shaking, and your enamel gets polished by the sheer force of your own confusion. It’s not just a workout; it’s a lifestyle. And if your teeth fall out? Well, that’s just the industry’s way of telling you to try harder. After all, nothing says "enviable physique" like a mouthful of empty gums and a pair of hollow plastic weights.
